entries.title: Second person charged with murder after man shoved from moving Red Line train
entries.summary: <p>A second person has been charged with murder in the death of 29-year-old Kyle Bickham, who was shoved from a moving CTA Red Line train earlier this month.</p><p>Katlar Parchman, 19, faces one count of first-degree murder, two additional murder counts, one count of aggravated battery of a transit employee, and one count of mob action, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Parchman was arrested Wednesday in the 200 block of North Keeler Avenue after investigators identified her as one of the people who allegedly helped push Bickham from a moving train Sept. 7 near the 69th Street station, police said.</p><p>A fight had broken out aboard the train before three people reportedly shoved Bickham onto the electrified third rail. He was then struck by another train and pronounced dead at the scene, according to police.</p><p>The Cook County medical examiner’s office determined Bickham died of multiple injuries and ruled his death a homicide.</p><p>A 15-year-old girl was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/13/15-year-old-girl-charged-murder-man-shoved-cta-red-line-train" target="_blank" >previously charged</a> with murder, mob action and felony assault of a transit employee in connection with Bickham’s death.</p><p>She was ordered detained during her first court appearance on Sept. 12, according to the Cook County state’s attorney’s office.</p><p>Area 1 detectives continue to investigate, police said.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Man, 41, dies after shot in face in South Shore
entries.summary: <p>A 41-year-old man was fatally shot in the South Shore neighborhood Saturday evening, Chicago police said.</p><p>The man was struck in the face by gunfire along the 7500 block of South Kingston Avenue at about 6:36 p.m., police said.</p><p>He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead, according to police.</p><p>Area detectives are investigating.<br></p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Kamilla Cardoso still believes in the Sky’s future — and coach Tyler Marsh
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — Another day, another beat down, this time at the hands of the Dream.</p><p>Despite the rough finish to the season, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> center <b>Kamilla Cardoso</b> remains confident about where the team is headed next year.</p><p>“I think we have a great squad,” she told the Sun-Times. “I think injuries messed us up a little bit, but I believe we have a great squad to make it to the playoffs and win a championship.”</p><p>Cardoso will enter the final year of her rookie contract next season. A championship is almost certainly still a ways off, but the Sky should benefit from better health and another year of development for their young core.</p><p>First, they must decide who will oversee that development.</p><p>Coach <b>Tyler Marsh</b> has been on the hot seat given the team was expected to make the playoffs. But Cardoso, who has praised Marsh’s offensive system throughout the season, gave him a vote of confidence.</p><p>“I think Tyler is an amazing coach,” she said. “I think he’s doing a great job and everything that he possibly can to help us. I do think he’s the right fit and I’m really excited to see what the future holds.”</p><p>If Marsh returns for a third season, he’ll have plenty of continuity to work with. Nine of the 13 players on the roster are under contract, and the Sky will have two first-round draft picks, one from the Dream and one from the Mystics.</p><p>The key will be making sure their young talent takes another step.</p><p>Cardoso had her best season yet, averaging 14.7 points and 8.7 rebounds, but parts of her game remain raw. She still doesn’t shoot much outside the paint, and foul trouble hurts her defensively.</p><p>This offseason, Cardoso is going to play in Project B, the five-on-five touring league launching in January. Before then, she’ll spend a few weeks at home in Brazil, then return to Chicago to train before Project B begins.</p><p><b>Respectable rookies</b></p><p>Three rookies in the starting lineup offered some support for Cardoso’s optimism. With veterans managing their injuries, rookies <b>Aicha Coulibaly</b> and <b>Gabriela Jaquez </b>made the most of their starts.</p><p>Coulibaly scored 11 points in the first half, continuing to show more polish on her drives. Jaquez<b> </b>looked more like the player from her first 15 games and finished with 14 points and 2 steals.</p><p>“Just being aggressive, trying to help the team win,” Jaquez said of her performance.</p><p>But the wheels came off when the Dream turned up the pressure in the second half, and the Sky fell 106-to-81.</p><p>Turnovers and poor three-point shooting once again hurt the Sky. So did their former star, <b>Angel Reese, </b>who<b> </b>scored 23 points on 9-13 shooting.</p><p><b>Taylor troubles</b></p><p>Taylor had another rough night. She picked up three early fouls and finished with two points on 1-8 shooting.</p><p>“I think one of Sydney’s growth areas is just not getting distracted when [her] shot’s not falling,” Marsh said. “There’s other ways that she can continue to be effective.”</p><p>Taylor did show off some nifty playmaking with two highlight-reel passes in the first half, but overall the Dream’s physicality gave her trouble.</p>
entries.author: Alissa Hirsh

entries.title: With Dream surging, Sky’s Angel Reese trade looks worse than ever
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — The last time the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> were in Atlanta in mid-July, there was at least a glimmer of hope in the trade that sent Angel Reese to the Dream for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028.</p><p>The Dream were slumping and had recently fallen as low as seventh in the standings. That meant the value of the Sky’s 2027 pick was rising, and maybe Reese wasn’t the missing piece Atlanta needed to reach the WNBA Finals after all.</p><p>With a week remaining in the regular season, that hope has vanished.</p><p>The Dream are now preparing for a championship run as top 4 team. And not only has Reese been their most consistent player, averaging 16.5 points, 12.4 rebounds and 1.8 steals, but she’s even in the conversation for her first All-WNBA selection.</p><p>She reminded the Sky of that Saturday night, leading the Dream to a 25-point rout.</p><p>Meanwhile, the Sky’s big roster revamp, headlined by the Reese trade, once again has them on the outside of the playoff picture.</p><p>A tough pill to swallow, especially since they don’t own their own 2027 pick and the one they’ll get from the Dream is likely to land late in the first round.</p><p>There is, at least, a caveat for Sky fans.</p><p>From a big picture perspective, this past offseason wasn’t really about swapping Reese for draft picks. It was swapping Reese for Rickea Jackson as the new face of the franchise. Jackson’s promising start lasted only four games before she tore her ACL.</p><p>So the final judgment on the Reese trade will have to include Jackson. Does she have a chance to become as good a player as Reese? Maybe. She’s already the better shot-creator and oozes talent and athleticism. After all, she was drafted three spots ahead of Reese in 2024, at No. 4.</p><p>But Jackson never totally proved herself during her first two years in Los Angeles, nor did she get the chance to in Chicago this season.</p><p>Reese already has, and then some.</p><p>She’s now a three-time All-Star, fresh off winning gold at the FIBA World Cup. She entered the league as a historically gifted rebounder and has quickly become one of its best defenders.</p><p>When asked to make Reese’s case for first-team All-Defensive honors, Dream coach Karl Smesko was shocked that anyone would need to hear it.</p><p>According to Smesko, all the advanced metrics point in favor of Reese. And if fancy statistics aren’t your thing, just watch her defend the pick-and-roll. At 6’3, she can both protect the rim and wreak havoc for guards, picking off their passes or slapping the ball out from under them.</p><p>“Case closed,” Smesko said.</p><p>The only question in Smesko's mind is whether she’ll be Defensive Player of the Year.</p><p>The Sky don’t have anyone in the All-Defensive conversation, much less the one for DPOY. Their team defense hasn’t been terrible this season; they rank eighth in defensive efficiency. But serious defenses in the WNBA need serious rim protection, and neither starting big, Kamilla Cardoso nor Azurá Stevens, has been physical enough around the rim.</p><p>Could Jackson help change that? She came into training camp sounding motivated to turn over a new leaf defensively, but it has never been her forte, and players don’t become elite defenders overnight.</p><p>Reese, by contrast, has been calling her shot since she was a rookie in Chicago. Defensive Player of the Year is where she has always believed she’s headed.</p><p>Sending away a star with that kind of mindset comes with consequences. Saturday night was one of them.</p>

entries.title: Review: Tool delivers an ear-blistering performance on Day 2 of Riot Fest

Giger-esque visuals can fester.</p><p>But singer Maynard James Keenan will take what he can get.</p><p>“Flight delayed. Set moved up. While bassist Justin Chancellor and drummer Danny Carey held down the rhythm section with unbelievable force, the winding atmospherics of guitarist Adam Jones were the real grease in the machine. working on new material. Yet they’re still riding out the fruits of their early labor, going back 30-plus years ago when they created a new kind of soundtrack in the ’90s that appealed as much to alt-rock kids as it did metalheads. They showed up in droves Saturday night to take in the set, as Tool was the sole headliner that represented the generation.</p><p>Making its Riot Fest debut, as the Saturday headliner, Tool was sandwiched in between younger rockers like Twenty One Pilots and Pierce the Veil, headliners of Friday and Sunday, respectively, yet earned its rightful place in the musical continuum.</p><p>As Tool wrapped with 1996’s hit “Ænema,” the sun finally starting to set, the prog rockers got their moment in the dark, where they truly shine.</p>

entries.title: 1 dead after shooting in North Lawndale
entries.summary:
An unidentified person was killed in a shooting in North Lawndale Saturday afternoon, Chicago police said.

Police said the male victim was in an alley along the 3900 block of West 18th Street at about 4:34 p.m. when someone approached him in an unknown vehicle and fired shots.

The victim was struck in the face, abdomen and leg, according to police.

He was initially taken to Mount Sinai Hospital and reported in critical condition before he was later pronounced dead, police said.

Area detectives are investigating.

entries.author: Georgia Nicols

entries.title: Fire fall to Eastern Conference-leading Nashville
entries.summary: <p>NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Sam Surridge scored in the first half and Brian Schwake finished off his league-leading 12th clean sheet of the season as Nashville SC clinched a playoff spot and remained unbeaten at home with a 3-0 victory over the Chicago Fire on Saturday night.</p><p>Eastern Conference-leading Nashville (17-3-6) leads the Supporters' Shield race and is the only team in the league unbeaten at home with a 12-0-1 record.</p><p>Surridge staked Nashville to a 1-0 lead in the 33rd minute and it stood through halftime.</p><p>Cristian Espinoza added an insurance goal in the 78th minute and Hany Mukhtar scored in the 87th to set the final margin.</p><p>It was the 16th goal of the campaign for Surridge, the fourth for Espinoza and the 11th for Mukhtar as the whole front line for Nashville found the net.</p><p>Schwake, a 25-year-old first-year starter, notched one save and has surrendered only 21 goals through 26 starts.</p><p>Chris Brady saved two shots for Chicago (11-8-6), which has lost two straight following a seven-match unbeaten streak.</p><p>The Fire handed Nashville its first loss of the season with a 1-0 victory at Soldier Field on April 4. Philip Zinckernagel scored 16 seconds into that match for the lone goal — the earliest scored in Fire history.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Chicago: At Charlotte FC on Saturday.</p><p>Nashville: Hosts Toronto FC on Saturday.</p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: Man critically wounded after being shot Saturday morning in Douglas
entries.summary: <p>A 47-year-old man was hospitalized for critical injuries early Saturday after he was shot in the Douglas neighborhood, Chicago police said.</p><p>Officers responded to a call of a person shot at about 3:29 a.m. along the 3600 block of South King Drive, where they found the man on the ground with a gunshot wound to the groin, police said.</p><p>Chicago Fire Department medics treated the man at the scene and took him to the University of Chicago Medical Center, according to police. He was listed in critical condition.</p><p>Area 1 detectives are investigating the incident.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Man critically injured in Garfield Park shooting
entries.summary: <p>A 45-year-old man was critically injured in a shooting in Garfield Park early Saturday, Chicago police said.</p><p>The man had been outside along the 3900 block of West Madison Street at about 7:07 a.m. when he was shot, according to police.</p><p>The wounded man took himself to Mount Sinai, where he was listed in critical condition, police said.</p><p>No other injuries were reported. Police said area detectives are investigating.</p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Notre Dame has little trouble getting past Michigan State
entries.summary: <p>SOUTH BEND, Ind. — C.J. Carr threw for 234 yards and ran for a touchdown, Nolan James Jr. rushed for 121 yards and a score, and No. 3 Notre Dame took control in the second half to beat Michigan State 27-10 on Saturday night.</p><p>It was the 13th straight victory dating to last season for the Fighting Irish — all by double digits. Coach Marcus Freeman broke the Notre Dame record for consecutive double-digit victories, exceeding the 12 by Knute Rockne from 1921-22.</p><p>Micah Gilbert had eight catches for 170 yards, the most yards for a Notre Dame receiver since 2019.</p><p>Carr's streak of 12 games with a passing touchdown ended, with the Fighting Irish (3-0) scoring all three TDs on short rushes.</p><p>Notre Dame outscored Michigan State 10-0 in the second half, limiting the Spartans (2-1) to 40 yards of offense over the final two quarters. Michigan State only had one play in Notre Dame territory in the second half, and a 9-yard sack sent the Spartans back into their own territory.</p><p>“It wasn’t perfect, as everybody saw, but it was a good victory and a hard-fought victory,” Freeman said. “Those are the type of victories that you’re going to have to win and find a way to win.”</p><p>Notre Dame punished the Spartans with four quarterback sacks, six tackles for loss and two interceptions, by Luke Talich and Adon Shuler.</p><p>“We make that a staple of our defense,” linebacker Drayk Bowen said. “We want to take the ball away. We want to be at least plus-two in every game. It’s intentional work in practice ... whether it’s a punch-out or we have a chance to intercept it.”</p><p>Carr's 3-yard run early in the fourth quarter made it 27-10. James scored on a 2-yard run in the first quarter, and Aneyas Williams ran it in from 1 yard out with 4:46 left in the second.</p><p>Williams' TD made it 17-3, but the Spartans closed within 17-10 by halftime. Cam Fancher, who platooned with Alessio Milivojevic at quarterback, scored on a 15-yard scramble.</p><p>Milivojevic was 9 of 17 passing for 123 yards and the two picks.</p><p>Michigan State coach Pat Fitzgerald said Notre Dame's quick start wounded the Spartans' chances for an upset.</p><p>“We had talked to them about avoiding the first-round knockout, and obviously we didn’t do a very good job of that, spotted them 10,” Fitzgerald said. “But we responded to that. We started moving the ball. We just sputtered. Credit Notre Dame. They have a darn good football team. We couldn’t give them the things we gave them and expect to win the game.</p><p>“I think we took a step today, from a maturity standpoint, but we did not from an execution standpoint.”</p><p><b>Irish shut down Spartans' run game</b></p><p>Notre Dame has held its last four opponents to fewer than 100 yards rushing. The Fighting Irish limited Michigan State to 44 yards on the ground — none in the second half. The Spartans' Cam Edwards entered the game leading the Big Ten in rushing and was fifth in the nation, averaging 125 yards per game. He finished with 12 carries for 38 yards.</p><p><b>The takeaway</b></p><p>Michigan State showed plenty of fight, and there should be optimism in East Lansing that the Spartans can finish with their first winning season since 2021.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Notre Dame: At Purdue next Saturday.</p><p>Michigan State: Hosts Nebraska next Saturday.</p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: Aidan Chiles and Joseph Himon lead Northwestern to rout of visiting Colorado
entries.summary: <p>Aidan Chiles passed to Joseph Himon II for three touchdowns and ran in two himself to lead Northwestern to a 41-7 rout of Colorado on Saturday night in Evanston.</p><p>Chiles finished with 241 yards on 17-for-22 passing and upped his season total to seven TDs – four passing and three rushing — in his first two games with the Wildcats (2-0). Chiles, a senior, made 20 starts for Michigan State before joining Northwestern during the offseason.</p><p>“There were some plays that certainly went off-script,” Northwestern coach David Braun said of his quarterback, “but his athleticism and his ability to keep the his eyes downfield, that's really hard to defend.”</p><p>Himon caught an 18-yard pass for his first TD, then a 25-yarder and a 3-yard toss as Northwestern (2-0) pulled away on a rainy evening two days after it announced an extension of Braun’s contract through the 2031 season.</p><p>In addition to 46 receiving yards, Himon, a graduate running back, added 28 on the ground. He has four TDs this season.</p><p>Asked about his on-field connection with Himon, Chiles said “keep it open.”</p><p>“We worked on it all week,” Chiles said. "We knew what we were gonna' get and we came out and executed.</p><p>“There were things that we saw that we knew we could exploit," Chiles added. ”I've talked to the coach, like he's given me the reins, like that's my job. I'm supposed to drive the car to lead the team and that's what I'm here to do."</p><p>Jackson Kleather kicked a pair of field goals in the fourth quarter and hit five extra-point attempts.</p><p>Colorado’s Julian “JuJu” Lewis threw for 168 yards and a touchdown to Joseph Williams on 19 for 29 passing as the Buffaloes (2-1) suffered their first loss after edging Georgia Tech, then routing Championship Subdivision foe Weber State last week.</p><p>Williams finished with 88 receiving yards and JaQuail Smith led the Buffaloes with 91 yards on the ground</p><p>The Buffaloes committed three key turnovers – two fumbles, one interception – in the first half. Two led to quick Northwestern scores.</p><p>The Wildcats led 21-0 at halftime.</p><p>Chiles ran left on a 1-yard keeper with 43 second left in the first quarter to open the scoring. Micah Welch fumbled at the Colorado 44-yard line to let Northwestern start the drive.</p><p>Lewis’ pass up the middle intended for Williams was intercepted by Braden Turner at the Colorado 40 midway through the second. Two plays later, Chiles hit a wide open Himon on the left side with an 18-yard pass to up the lead to 14-0.</p><p>Damian Henderson II was stopped, getting only one yard, on a fourth-and-2 rush attempt at the NU 28 on the Buffaloes next drive.</p><p>Chiles ran the ball in from the Colorado 3 for his second touchdown of the night with 59 seconds left in the half to extend it to 21-0.</p><p>Williams took off alone down the right side for a 50-yard touchdown dash after taking Lewis’ pass at midfield on the fourth play of the second half to complete a quick 66-yard drive for the Buffaloes' first touchdown.</p><p>The Wildcats and Chiles countered to make it 28-7 midway through the third when he found Himon again, this time with a pass up the middle. Chiles hit Himon with a 3-yard toss with 3:15 left in the third to extend it to 35-7.</p><h3><b>Yards don’t matter</b></h3><p>Colorado posted 348 total yards (to Northwestern's 423) and narrowly lead in that stat at the half. Still Northwestern allowed only seven points.</p><p>Braun pointed to a“bending-and-not breaking” element of his defense, and its ability to force and exploit turnovers.</p><p>“Looking at yardage stats is for losers,” he said. “At the end of the day, it does not dictate winning.”</p><p>Braun did say his team has plenty to “clean up,” including tackling better.</p><h3><b>The takeaway</b></h3><p>Colorado: The Buffaloes were hurt by the early turnovers before Lewis was intercepted again the fourth quarter.</p><p>Northwestern: The Chiles-Himon combo was unstoppable, and Northwestern committed only one turnover. Saturday’s contest was the last played at 12,000-seat Martin Stadium, the Wildcats on-campus home since 2024. They’ll open the new 35,000-seat Ryan Field on Friday, Oct. 2 when they host Penn State.</p><h3><b>Up next</b></h3><p>Colorado: Opens its Big 12 schedule next Saturday at Baylor.</p><p>Northwestern: Faces defending national champion Indiana in Bloomington, Indiana next Saturday to open its Big Ten schedule.</p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: Daniel Palencia looks like himself again with 2 dominant innings in Cubs' victory
entries.summary: <p>CINCINNATI — Daniel Palenica appears to have recaptured his form just in time.</p><p>Palencia, who had 22 saves and a 2.91 ERA last season, looked the best he has this season, retiring all six batters he faced in the sixth and seventh innings Saturday in the Cubs’ 5-2 victory against the Reds. He struck out three and averaged 99.5 mph on his fastball, hitting 100 four times. Palenica threw 20 pitches, 15 for strikes.</p><p>And it all happened with the Cubs nursing a one-run lead. It wasn’t the same as getting the last three outs, but it was high-leverage nonetheless as the team inched closer to clinching a wild-card berth.</p><p>“Twenty pitches, probably executed 19,” manager Craig Counsell said. “It was a good sign and an important sign.”</p><p>The Cubs haven’t had a regular closer since Jacob Webb lost the job late last month. Perhaps in the final week of the season, Palenica can reclaim the role he had at the beginning of the season and keep it in the postseason, where he had five scoreless outings out of six last year.</p><p>“The bottom line is Danny’s healthy now, and again, just keep getting him out there, and it’ll click,” Counsell said. “He’s a talented pitcher. I felt like a broken record saying, ‘Just keep getting him out there.’ But that’s what you do with talented players. You keep putting them out there, and they’ll figure it out.”</p><p>“He’s more and more time away from being on the IL,” starter Matthew Boyd said of Palencia, who missed time with a strained left oblique and elbow inflammation. “That’s huge. Those reps, you can’t replicate them. Tonight was exactly who he is, and it was awesome to see.”</p><p>Boyd allowed two runs (one earned) in five innings before Palenica entered. Aaron Civale followed with two-thirds of an inning, then Ryan Zeferjahn with one before Ryan Rolison earned his third save by retiring one batter.</p><p>Rolison is among 14 Cubs with a save this season. Perhaps Palencia will be the only one in the postseason.</p><h3>Happ handling platoon</h3><p>One reason the Cubs acquired Tyrone Taylor before the trade deadline was because Ian Happ has struggled badly against left-handed pitching. The switch-hitting Happ has an .826 OPS against righties and a .494 mark against lefties. The right-handed-hitting Taylor has a .906 OPS against lefties.</p><p>That has relegated Happ, a four-time Glove Glove-winning left fielder, to a platoon role. With Reds lefty Nick Lodolo on the mound, Taylor started in left. Happ pinch-hit for him in the eighth when righty Pierce Johnson entered.</p><p>“That’s just the way it is, unfortunately,” Counsell said. “All of us here have performance standards that we got to live up to. It’s not for lack of trying. But on the flip side of that, how Ian’s handled that part of it has been for the betterment of the team.</p><p>“He always has that on his [mind], and it’s important to him. He gets it. It’s not what Ian wants; he wants to be in there every day. But I think he understands right now against left-handed pitching, Tyrone’s the better option.”</p><h3>Steele decision coming</h3><p>Left-hander Justin Steele struck out five in two scorless innings Friday at Triple-A Iowa, his fourth rehab appearance in his recovery from surgery on his left elbow. He didn’t allow a hit and walked one.</p><p>“It was certainly encouraging,” Counsell said. “He flew back to Chicago; we’ll see him on Tuesday. We’ve got some discussions to have there.”</p><p>If the Cubs think Steele, who hasn’t pitched in a big-league game since April 7, 2025, can help in the postseason, they could put him on the taxi squad, allowing him to travel and serve as an emergency replacement.</p><p>“We’ll see what we think going into the last week,” Counsell said. “There’s a lot of things that factor into it.”</p><p>Elsewhere, right-handed reliever Trent Thornton will pitch Sunday for Iowa in his rehab from a sprained left ankle.</p><h3>The opposition view</h3><p>Last year at this time, the Reds were in the middle of sweeping the Cubs in a four-game series on their way to an 8-3 finish that clinched them a wild-card spot on the last day of the season. This season, they’re trying to play spoiler.</p><p>“I’m jealous,” Reds manager Terry Francona said of other teams, including the Cubs, fighting for playoff spots. “[Friday] night, we were looking at the scoreboard, like [bleep] man, that feeling of anxiety, I kind of miss that.”</p>
